text: Howard Okonjo's board mandate included a standing requirement: every risk this program surfaces has to be tracked somewhere auditable, with an owner and a decision attached. That's a GRC risk register, and building Hartwell's first real one is this lesson's job.

A risk register only earns its keep if every row carries the same columns: Risk ID, Description, Likelihood, Impact, Owner, Treatment, Compensating control, Status, and Review date. Owner is always a named person, never just a team.

Mara opens the register with five real risks. R-03 flags that Hartwell's break-glass emergency access has no automatic expiration. R-05 schedules the quarterly compliance audit of the OT and SCADA segment's standing access -- the exact audit the next lesson covers.
This register isn't paperwork. By Lesson 17 it gets a sixth row, written with a real finding Lessons 11 and 12 are about to produce.
